entities.summary: Titus Tarquinius was the eldest son of Lucius Tarquinius Superbus, the last king of Rome, who played a significant role in the downfall of the Roman monarchy. Born around 600 BCE, Titus Tarquinius was instrumental in the overthrow of his father and the eventual establishment of the Roman Republic. Despite his involvement in the tumultuous events that led to the end of the Roman monarchy, Titus Tarquinius remains a somewhat enigmatic figure. He was a key figure in the Roman Revolution, which was marked by the expulsion of the last king and the establishment of a new system of governance. The event had a profound impact on the Roman state, leading to the creation of a new constitution and the rise of the Roman Republic. The legacy of Titus Tarquinius continues to be felt in the Roman state, with many historians arguing that his actions helped to pave the way for the eventual rise of the Roman Empire. In the words of the Roman historian Livy, 'Titus Tarquinius was a man of great courage and cunning, who was willing to do whatever it took to secure his place in history.'
